slides.title: What your diploma pays
slides.sub: 4 paths after high school, ranked by median weekly pay in 2025 (full-time workers 25 and older).

slides.heading: #1 Bachelor's degree
body: About $82,000 a year (HFLIC math: weekly pay x 52).
Unemployment rate: 2.8%. A master's pays $1,876 a week.

slides.heading: #2 Associate's degree
body: That's $169 a week more than a high school diploma.

slides.heading: #3 College, no degree
body: Starting college without finishing adds only $96 a week over a diploma.

slides.heading: #4 High school diploma
body: Without a diploma, it's $770 a week and 6.1% unemployment.

slides.takeaway: Whatever path you pick, finish it. The pay jump comes with the credential.

posts.caption:
What does each path after high school pay? BLS median weekly earnings for full-time workers 25 and older in 2025:

1. Bachelor's degree: $1,578 a week (unemployment 2.8%)
2. Associate's degree: $1,135 (3.0%)
3. Some college, no degree: $1,062 (3.8%)
4. High school diploma: $966 (4.3%)

Rough HFLIC math (weekly pay x 52): a bachelor's works out to about $82,000 a year, and a diploma to about $50,000. Starting college without finishing adds only $96 a week over a diploma. These are medians, not guarantees, and BLS notes the 2025 averages leave out October 2025.

Data: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Education pays, 2025 (Sept. 2026).
